title: Value preservation under constant removal
statement: Let $n>0$, let $C$ be a directed acyclic Boolean circuit on $n$ input vertices whose gates have distinct arguments, whose NOT gates each read exactly one vertex, and whose gates each read at most two vertices. For every input assignment $x:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ and every vertex $v<n+|C|$, the value at the shifted vertex in the circuit obtained by adjoining the three-gate constant prefix and transforming the gates equals the value at $v$ in $C$; values at indices beyond the available list are interpreted as false.
hypotheses_covered: Circuit has well-formed gates with distinct arguments
Every NOT gate has exactly one argument
Every gate has at most two arguments
An input assignment to the $n$ input vertices
